styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a stone-framed stair opening with a dark interior and visible step bands. Its measured facts match the paving reference: 7 visible tones per tile against 7, 0% near-flat coverage against 0%, and 87% neutral dark edge pixels against 80%. The grass reference has only 3 visible tones, so the candidate is not thin next to it. The frame has a light face, mid tone and dark edge, and the steps step down in value, which gives about 5 shading steps. The outline is a neutral dark grey, but the paving reference uses the same neutral grey, and much of the form is separated by value alone, so I call it mixed rather than a uniform sticker line. Texture is modest: the frame and steps carry some stone-grain dots but less than the cobbled paving. Overall it is slightly lower in richness by eye but acceptable next to the paving reference, since the numbers equal it and no large flat fills show.
